source_name: ECB retail payments / instant payments and IPR hub
why_relevant: Policy hub for the Instant Payments Regulation and the euro area SCT Inst indicator; pointer to the Eurosystem's monitoring artefacts that shape SK bank/PSP roadmaps and terminal/acceptance economics.

source_name: NBS — Slovak-language relay of ECB payment/cash findings (aktuality)
source_subtype: national central bank news relay of supranational output
why_relevant: Národná banka Slovenska republishes ECB SPACE / payment-attitudes findings in Slovak, often with SK-specific commentary the ECB report does not foreground. Also the best source of correct Slovak terminology for downstream local-language searching.

source_name: ECB banknote circulation statistics (Slovak-language page)
why_relevant: One of the few ECB statistical pages actually served in Slovak. Euro banknote circulation by denomination is the supply-side counterpart to SPACE demand-side cash usage and to ATM withdrawal volumes.

source_name: SUERF Policy Briefs — ECB-authored payment/cash research summaries
why_relevant: SUERF publishes short, citable briefs by ECB economists distilling SPACE and CBDC/cash-demand research (e.g. Nocciola & Zamora-Pérez on CBDC demand). Faster-moving and more interpretive than the ECB reports; good for early signals on euro-area cash-usage direction that condition SK.

source_name: ECB Statistical Data Warehouse (legacy SDW) — Slovakia payments country tables
why_relevant: The predecessor portal still surfaces the 'Country tables: Euro area — Payments Statistics — Slovakia' node, which can expose discontinued annual series (pre-2022) that are awkward to locate in the new Data Portal.

source_name: ECB Data Portal — discontinued annual payments statistics
why_relevant: Holds the pre-2022 annual SK payment/terminal/card history under the old ECB/2013/43 framework. Required to build a long-run Slovak ATM and POS terminal series that predates the semi-annual regime.

source_name: Eurostat Data Browser — Financial activities over the internet (isoc_ec_ifi20)
why_relevant: Harmonised annual EU survey indicator on individuals using internet banking / online financial activities, with SK breakouts by age, education, degree of urbanisation. Core demand-side digital-payments series for Slovakia comparable across EU27.

source_name: Eurostat — Individuals: internet activities (isoc_ci_ac_i)
why_relevant: Long historical series (pre-2020) of internet activities including internet banking for SK; needed to build a continuous time series alongside isoc_ec_ifi20 which starts 2020.

source_name: Eurostat — Internet purchases by individuals (isoc_ec_ib20 / legacy isoc_ec_ibuy)
why_relevant: E-commerce volume and category detail for SK — the demand pipe that drives card-not-present and online payment acceptance; useful proxy for e-commerce payment market sizing.

source_name: Eurostat Statistics Explained — Digital society statistics at regional level
why_relevant: Editorial layer that names the exact dataset codes and NUTS2 regional cuts (e.g. Bratislavský kraj vs other SK regions for internet banking) — a fast route to the right underlying tables and to regional payment-adoption gaps.

source_name: Eurostat Statistics Explained (Slovak edition) — e.g. Beginners: Government finance statistics /sk
why_relevant: Confirms Eurostat publishes Slovak-language explainer pages; gives the official Slovak statistical vocabulary (bezhotovostné platby, platobná bilancia, štatistika) that can be reused as search terms against SK-language re-publishers of Eurostat data.

source_name: data.europa.eu — official EU open data portal (Slovak interface)
why_relevant: Federated catalogue harvesting Eurostat plus Slovak national open-data portals; the single best discovery surface for machine-readable SK datasets touching payments, financial access and digital economy. Slovak UI gives local-language faceted search.

source_name: data.europa.eu — Slovakia country insights (open data maturity)
why_relevant: Maps which Slovak public bodies publish open data and how mature the SK portal ecosystem is — tells us where SK payment/financial datasets are likely to appear and how reliably they are refreshed.

source_name: World Bank Global Findex Database (2025 edition landing page)
why_relevant: Only globally comparable demand-side survey of account ownership, card ownership/use, digital payment made-or-received, and now digital connectivity. Slovakia is covered as a high-income economy; gives triangulation against ECB/NBS supply-side stats.

source_name: World Bank Microdata Library — Global Findex 2025 survey microdata (141 economies)
why_relevant: Respondent-level microdata allows custom SK cuts (by age, income quintile, rural/urban, gender) that the published indicators do not expose — e.g. card use among lower-income SK adults.

source_name: FRED (St. Louis Fed) — Slovak Republic geographical outreach series (SVKFCAANUM)
why_relevant: Mirror of IMF FAS SK access-point series in a far more automation-friendly wrapper (stable series IDs, CSV, free API key). Useful as a resilient fallback when IMF/World Bank endpoints change.

source_name: BIS Data Portal — Financial market infrastructures and critical service providers (CPMI_FMI)
why_relevant: Red Book FMI statistics on payment systems, CSDs and CCPs — participation counts and settlement volumes. Relevant to SK only via euro area / TARGET-level rows, but establishes the methodological standard used by NBS reporting.

source_name: BIS CPMI — Red Book statistics methodology (CPMI d168)
why_relevant: Definitive definitions for payment-statistics concepts (POS terminal, cash withdrawal, e-money, cashless payment) used across BIS, ECB and national reporting. Essential for making SK figures from different aggregators comparable without double counting.

source_name: BIS CPMI — Payment, clearing and settlement in various countries (country pages index)
why_relevant: Index of narrative country/jurisdiction Red Book chapters; the route to confirm exactly how the euro area chapter treats SK and which national chapters exist. Also snowballs to national central bank payment-system publications.

source_name: European Commission — Digital Decade DESI visualisation tool and datasets
why_relevant: DG CNECT's composite digital-economy indicator system with SK values and EU-average benchmarks across digital skills, connectivity, business digitalisation and digital public services — the standard context frame for arguing SK digital-payment readiness. Downloadable indicator datasets.

source_name: European Commission — Slovakia Digital Decade Country Report (annual factpage)
why_relevant: Annual narrative + indicator assessment of SK digital performance with EU comparison, including take-up of digital public services and business digitalisation — provides interpretation and policy trajectory around SK payment digitalisation.

source_name: EU Payment Observatory — Indicators Database / Data Mapper (DG GROW, run with CEPS)
why_relevant: Interactive EEA-wide database of commercial payment behaviour (payment terms, delays, B2B vs B2G) with SK member-state cuts, updated yearly. Distinct from retail card statistics but directly relevant to B2B payments and working-capital dynamics in the SK payments market.

source_name: European Court of Auditors — Special Report 01/2025: Digital payments in the EU
why_relevant: Independent EU audit of digital-payments policy that compiles cross-member-state uptake figures (incl. instant payments) and audits the Commission's own data. Useful as an audited secondary compilation and as a pointer to the underlying datasets the Commission holds.

source_name: European Commission DG FISMA newsroom — instant payments item pages
why_relevant: DG FISMA's own dissemination channel for retail-payments policy documents, impact assessments and supporting data annexes (which often contain member-state tables including SK uptake of SCT Inst).

source_name: European Commission Library — Fintech / Digital Finance statistics and data guide
why_relevant: Librarian-curated inventory of EU and international statistics sources on payments and digital finance — a high-yield snowball surface listing aggregators we might otherwise miss, with notes on coverage and access.

source_name: DBnomics — Eurostat dataset mirrors (isoc_ci_ac_i, isoc_ec_ib20)
why_relevant: Third-party aggregator mirroring Eurostat series with a uniform free API and series-level provenance; useful for rapid prototyping and as a fallback when the Eurostat API is rate-limited or restructured. Not authoritative — always reconcile to Eurostat.

source_name: Trading Economics — EU/Slovakia Eurostat-derived internet banking indicator page
why_relevant: Commercial re-publisher of the Eurostat internet-banking series; occasionally surfaces indicator pages faster than the primary and provides quick charts, but is paywalled/licence-restricted for systematic reuse.

source_name: Finančná správa SR — Open Data portál (ODFS), kategória eKasa / e-cash register
why_relevant: Single most valuable non-central-bank source in this cell: ~10 recurring datasets from the eKasa online cash-register system — počet vytvorených pokladničných dokladov (weekly and monthly), vývoj tržieb v eurách, tržby/doklady by self-governing region, tržby/doklady by SK NACE2 industry code, count of registered online (ORP) and virtual (VRP) cash registers. This is till-level turnover and transaction-count evidence for the whole SK retail/HORECA economy, published by the tax authority rather than NBS, and is the natural denominator against which card/POS transaction volumes can be benchmarked.

source_name: Finančná správa SR — Open Data portál (ODFS) root catalogue
why_relevant: Pointer/hub listing all Financial Administration open-data categories (výkon správy daní, informačné zoznamy z Portálu FS, index daňovej spoľahlivosti, registrácia daňových subjektov, štátna pomoc, účtovné závierky). Snowballing this catalogue is the cheapest way to find further fiscal datasets that touch merchant populations and cash-vs-cashless behaviour.
